name: Aaron
description: High Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness

points: Moses pressed, Send, I pray thee, by the hand of him whom thou wilt send; and the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses. Is not Aaron the Levite thy brother? I know that he can speak well; he spoke the Hebrew of the people fluently.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

points: The LORD sent Aaron into the wilderness to meet Moses, and he met him in the mount of God and kissed him; Aaron believed right away. Moses told Aaron all the words of the LORD and all the signs.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

points: Moses and Aaron went in and told Pharaoh, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Let my people go, that they may hold a feast unto me in the wilderness. That feast was the Passover.

note.label: Exodus 5: Let My People Go

points: The king of Egypt said, Wherefore do ye, Moses and Aaron, let the people from their works? get you unto your burdens. That is the standing complaint of the oppressor: the prophets are pulling the people from their labor and getting their hopes up that their God will deliver them.

note.label: Exodus 5: Let My People Go

points: Chapter 6 is dealing with the genealogy: the families of Reuben, Simeon, and Levi, and out of Levi came Moses and Aaron. Levi begat Kohath, Kohath begat Amram, and Amram took Jochebed to wife, and she bare him Aaron and Moses.

note.label: Exodus 6: The Promise Renewed and the Generations of Moses and Aaron

points: These are that Aaron and Moses to whom the Lord said, Bring out the children of Israel from the land of Egypt; these are they which spake to Pharaoh king of Egypt.

note.label: Exodus 6: The Promise Renewed and the Generations of Moses and Aaron

points: The Lord made Moses a god to Pharaoh, and Aaron his brother was his prophet. Moses was as God and Aaron was the mouthpiece, because Moses kept saying he was of uncircumcised lips.

note.label: Exodus 7: Aaron's Rod and the River Turned to Blood

points: It was Aaron who cast down the rod before Pharaoh, and it became a serpent. A lot of people to this day say it was Moses with the rod, because they do not read the Bible; Moses was telling Aaron what to do, and it was Aaron's rod that turned into the serpent.

note.label: Exodus 7: Aaron's Rod and the River Turned to Blood

points: Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters, and the frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt. With this second plague the Most High was mocking Heqet, the Egyptian idol god of the frogs.

note.label: Exodus 8: Frogs, Lice, and Swarms of Flies

points: So Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron and said, Entreat the Lord that he may take away the frogs. Why did Pharaoh not call on Heqet, the god of frogs? He had to go to the Lord.

note.label: Exodus 8: Frogs, Lice, and Swarms of Flies

points: When the judgment got real, Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron in haste and confessed, I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you. Everything had been eaten by the locusts, and now he begged that this death only be taken from him.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

points: The feast days commemorate the Most High delivering his people and bringing judgment on their enemies; that is the same pattern the feast of dedication commemorates. The people bowed the head and worshipped, and the children of Israel went and did as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron.

note.label: Exodus 12: The Lord's Passover

points: The last time Pharaoh saw Moses he threatened to kill him if he ever saw his face again; now he called for Moses and Aaron by night, saying, Rise up, get you forth from among my people, go, serve the Lord as ye have said, take your flocks and your herds, and bless me also. Touch not mine anointed, and do my prophets no harm; the man who thought he could threaten the servant of the Most High had a complete change of tone.

note.label: Exodus 12: The Lord's Passover

points: Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel, and all the women went out after her with timbrels and with dances, answering the song: sing ye to the Lord, for he hath triumphed gloriously.

note.label: Exodus 15: The Song of Moses: The Lord Is a Man of War

points: After they complained, after they murmured, guess what God did? All right, here's some water. Here you go. And the whole congregation still murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness.

note.label: Jude 1:16

points: Moses stood on the top of the hill with the rod of God in his hand: when Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed; when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed. His hands were heavy, so they set a stone under him, and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands, the one on the one side and the other on the other side, steady until the going down of the sun; and Joshua discomfited Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: When Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed; when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed. Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands until the going down of the sun. Moses was about eighty years old holding a rod above his head all day; the fathers were mighty men, stronger than we are today.

note.label: Exodus 17: Water Out of the Rock and War With Amalek

points: Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel were called up to worship afar off, and Moses alone came near the Lord.

note.label: Exodus 24: The Blood of the Covenant

points: Aaron and his sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar are taken from among the children of Israel to minister unto the Most High in the priest's office.

note.label: Exodus 28: Holy Garments for Glory and for Beauty

points: The Most High commanded holy garments to be made for Aaron for glory and for beauty. Garments were ordained for the men of Israel; when the world hears Deuteronomy 22:5 and asks why the men wear garments, the answer is here: the most holy and regarded men of the nation, the priests, were arrayed in long garments down to the foot.

note.label: Exodus 28: Holy Garments for Glory and for Beauty

points: Only the wise hearted, whom the Most High filled with the spirit of wisdom, could make Aaron's garments. The garment is heavenly, mapped out for Moses to create on earth; the Lord had to be dealing with a man in a certain way, putting the spirit within him, for him to be able to create that glory and beauty. It cannot be duplicated.

note.label: Exodus 28: Holy Garments for Glory and for Beauty

points: The garments to be made: a breastplate, an ephod, a robe, a broidered coat, a mitre, and a girdle, holy garments for Aaron and his sons to minister in the priest's office.

note.label: Exodus 28: Holy Garments for Glory and for Beauty

points: Two onyx stones are engraved with the names of the children of Israel, six names on one stone and six on the other according to their birth, set in ouches of gold upon the shoulders of the ephod; Aaron bare the names of the tribes before the Lord upon his two shoulders for a memorial.

note.label: Exodus 28: Holy Garments for Glory and for Beauty

points: Aaron shall bear the names of the children of Israel in the breastplate of judgment upon his heart when he goeth in unto the holy place, for a memorial before the Lord continually. The Most High was all about His nation being represented: put Israel on your chest when you go into the temple.

note.label: Exodus 28: Holy Garments for Glory and for Beauty

points: The Urim and the Thummim go in the breastplate of judgment, upon Aaron's heart before the Lord; Aaron bears the judgment of the children of Israel upon his heart continually.

note.label: Exodus 28: Holy Garments for Glory and for Beauty

points: A plate of pure gold engraved like a signet, HOLINESS TO THE LORD, on a blue lace upon the forefront of the mitre, always upon Aaron's forehead, that Aaron may bear the iniquity of the holy things of the children of Israel and that they may be accepted before the Lord.

note.label: Exodus 28: Holy Garments for Glory and for Beauty

points: The broidered coat of fine linen, the mitre of fine linen, and the girdle of needlework; and for Aaron's sons coats, girdles, and bonnets, for glory and for beauty, to be anointed and consecrated in.

note.label: Exodus 28: Holy Garments for Glory and for Beauty

points: Linen breeches to cover their nakedness, from the loins even unto the thighs, upon Aaron and his sons when they come near the altar to minister, that they bear not iniquity and die: a statute for ever unto him and his seed after him.

note.label: Exodus 28: Holy Garments for Glory and for Beauty

points: The garments are put upon Aaron, the coat, the robe of the ephod, the ephod, and the breastplate, with the curious girdle; the mitre upon his head and the holy crown upon the mitre; the anointing oil poured upon his head; and his sons in coats, girdles, and bonnets. The priest's office shall be theirs for a perpetual statute: thou shalt consecrate Aaron and his sons.

Ecclesiasticus records the same consecration: Moses anointed him with holy oil, an everlasting covenant to Aaron and to his seed so long as the heavens should remain, to minister unto Him, execute the office of the priesthood, offer the sacrifices, and teach Jacob the testimonies and inform Israel in His laws. The priest's job was the offerings and teaching the nation the law, statutes, and commandments.

That is why leadership today is not walking around requiring Levite lineage of Aaron. Christ is the high priest now, and the nation is a whole nation of kings and priests; Malachi and Hebrews are two good books to study on the changing of the priesthood, against the doctrine that the Aaronic covenant could never change.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: The second ram is the ram of consecration: its blood is put upon the tip of the right ear of Aaron and of his sons, upon the thumb of their right hand and the great toe of their right foot, and sprinkled upon the altar round about; the blood and the anointing oil are sprinkled upon Aaron, his garments, his sons, and their garments, and he shall be hallowed.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: The bread and the parts of the ram are put in the hands of Aaron and his sons and waved for a wave offering before the Lord, then burnt upon the altar; and the breast of the wave offering and the shoulder of the heave offering are sanctified for Aaron and his sons by a statute for ever. There go the wave offering and the heave offering, which you will read about throughout the first five books, Leviticus predominantly.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: The tabernacle shall be sanctified by His glory, and Aaron and his sons sanctified to minister in the priest's office; for the Most High to enter and deal with Israel, everything had to be sanctified. That was serious.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: Aaron burned sweet incense on it every morning when he dressed the lamps, and again at even when he lighted the lamps, a perpetual incense before the Lord throughout the generations; it burned continually, morning and evening.

note.label: Exodus 30: The Altar of Incense and the Holy Anointing Oil

points: Aaron made an atonement upon the horns of it once in a year with the blood of the sin offering of atonements; it is most holy unto the Lord. This altar served the day of atonement.

note.label: Exodus 30: The Altar of Incense and the Holy Anointing Oil

points: They made the cloths of service, the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons to minister in the priest's office, the anointing oil, and the sweet incense for the holy place, according to all that the Lord commanded.

note.label: Exodus 31: Bezaleel and Aholiab, and the Sabbath Sign

points: We are the same people who saw God use Moses to split the Red Sea right in front of us. It was not even long after; Moses said I will be right back, and the people gathered themselves unto Aaron: up, make us gods which shall go before us.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

points: When the people saw that Moses delayed to come down out of the mount, they gathered unto Aaron: Up, make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses, we wot not what is become of him. Any time deliverance did not come when Israel wanted it, the nation rebelled, and Moses and the leadership got the blame; the same spirit is against the leadership of Israel to this day.

note.label: Exodus 32: The Golden Calf at Horeb

points: Aaron said break off the golden earrings which are in the ears of your wives, of your sons, and of your daughters. Men and women both wore earrings in the scriptures, and it is not sin.

note.label: Exodus 32: The Golden Calf at Horeb

points: Moses said unto Aaron, What did this people unto thee, that thou hast brought so great a sin upon them? He had left Aaron in charge, and came back to a camp deep in wickedness.

note.label: Exodus 32: The Golden Calf at Horeb

points: Aaron answered, Let not the anger of my lord wax hot: thou knowest the people, that they are set on mischief; they said make us gods, I cast the gold into the fire, and there came out this calf. A leader cannot blame the congregation, the same excuse Saul gave; the charge has to be carried.

note.label: Exodus 32: The Golden Calf at Horeb

points: The people were naked, for Aaron had made them naked unto their shame among their enemies. That is the same nakedness of Genesis 3, the shame of sin uncovered.

note.label: Exodus 32: The Golden Calf at Horeb

points: The list runs through the whole work: the tabernacle, his tent, his covering, his taches, boards, bars, pillars, and sockets; the ark of the covenant with the staves and the mercy seat, and the vail of the covering; the table with his staves and vessels and the shewbread; the candlestick, which is the menorah, with his lamps and the oil for the light; the incense altar; the altar of burnt offering, where the burnt offering was burnt, with his brasen grate; the laver; the hangings of the court; and the cloths of service, the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons, to minister in the priest's office.

note.label: Exodus 35: The Sabbath and the Willing Hearted Offering

points: This is the sum of the tabernacle: a collection was taken in order to fund the building of the tabernacle and the service of building it, counted according to the commandment of Moses by the hand of Ithamar son to Aaron the priest.

note.label: Exodus 38: The Altar, the Court, and the Sum of the Offering

points: Chapter 39 is the application of the instructions of chapter 28: the holy garments for Aaron the priest, the clothes of service to do service in the holy place, made of the blue, purple, and scarlet as the Lord commanded Moses.

note.label: Exodus 39: The Holy Garments and the Names of the Children of Israel

points: The meat offering is of fine flour, with oil poured upon it and frankincense put thereon; the priest burns his handful of it as a memorial upon the altar, an offering made by fire of a sweet savour unto the Lord, and the remnant belongs to Aaron and his sons.

note.label: Leviticus 2: The Meat Offering of Fine Flour

points: That which is left of the meat offering is Aaron's and his sons', a thing most holy of the offerings of the Lord made by fire.

note.label: Leviticus 2: The Meat Offering of Fine Flour

points: The peace offering could be of the herd or of the flock, a lamb or a goat, male or female without blemish, unlike the burnt offering of chapter 1, which was a male. The offerer laid his hand upon the head of his offering and killed it at the door of the tabernacle, and Aaron's sons sprinkled the blood upon the altar round about.

note.label: Leviticus 3: The Peace Offering Without Blemish

points: This is the offering of Aaron and of his sons in the day when he is anointed: the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour for a meat offering perpetual, half in the morning and half at night, baked with oil in a pan. The meat offering is again actual flour, grain.

note.label: Leviticus 6: The Trespass Offering and the Fire That Shall Never Go Out

points: The wave breast and the heave shoulder were given to Aaron the priest and his sons by a statute for ever; this is how the priests ate from the peace offerings. Leviticus 10 returns to these portions, the wave breast and heave shoulder given to Aaron and his sons and daughters; chapters 6 through 10 explain the offerings.

note.label: Leviticus 7: Christ Our Peace Offering

points: Take Aaron and his sons with him, and the garments, and the anointing oil, and a bullock for the sin offering, and two rams, and a basket of unleavened bread; and all the congregation was gathered unto the door of the tabernacle.

note.label: Leviticus 8: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: Moses washed Aaron and his sons with water, and put upon him the coat, the girdle, the robe, and the ephod, and he put the breastplate upon him, and in the breastplate the Urim and the Thummim.

note.label: Leviticus 8: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: Moses anointed the tabernacle and all that was therein, sprinkled the altar seven times, and poured of the anointing oil upon Aaron's head, and anointed him, to sanctify him, to set him apart.

This is what David is going back to in the psalm: behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity; it is like the precious ointment upon the head, that ran down upon the beard, even Aaron's beard, down to the skirts of his garments. That oil could be poured on no one but the high priest; that is how precious unity among the people is to be.

note.label: Leviticus 8: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: Moses slew the other ram, the ram of consecration, and put the blood upon the tip of Aaron's right ear, upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot, and the same for his sons.

note.label: Leviticus 8: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: Moses sprinkled the anointing oil and the blood upon Aaron and his garments and upon his sons and their garments, and sanctified them. They boiled the flesh at the door of the tabernacle and ate it there with the bread of consecration, and abode at the door of the tabernacle day and night seven days, until the days of their consecration were at an end.

note.label: Leviticus 8: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: Moses said unto Aaron, go unto the altar, and offer thy sin offering and thy burnt offering, and make an atonement for thyself, and for the people. The priest had to make an atonement for himself first, and then offer the offering of the people.

note.label: Leviticus 9: The Glory of the Lord Appears

points: Aaron dipped his finger in the blood and put it upon the horns of the altar, burnt the fat and kidneys and caul, the guts, upon the altar, and the flesh and the hide he burnt with fire without the camp; you keep reading it over and over, without the camp.

note.label: Leviticus 9: The Glory of the Lord Appears

points: The breasts and the right shoulder Aaron waved for a wave offering before the LORD, a washed piece lifted and waved, as Moses commanded.

note.label: Leviticus 9: The Glory of the Lord Appears

points: Aaron lifted up his hand toward the people and blessed them, and came down from offering the sin offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offerings; and Moses and Aaron went into the tabernacle, and came out and blessed the people.

note.label: Leviticus 9: The Glory of the Lord Appears

points: Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took either of them his censer, put fire therein and incense thereon, and offered strange fire before the Lord, which he commanded them not; and fire went out from the Lord and devoured them.

The instructions for the incense were already given: Aaron shall burn sweet incense every morning and at even, a perpetual incense before the Lord throughout your generations, and ye shall offer no strange incense thereon. There were instructions on what could be burned and what could not; the strange fire is that Nadab and Abihu put strange incense before the Lord.

note.label: Leviticus 10: Strange Fire and the Charge of the Priesthood

points: “Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took either of them his censer, and put fire therein”. These are high priests. They put the fire in the censers and incense on it. “and offered strange fire before the Lord, which he commanded them not.” He didn't command them to make that fire.

note.label: When Good Intentions Lead To Bad Judgement In Israel

points: Then Moses said unto Aaron, this is what the Lord spake: I will be sanctified in them that come nigh me, and before all the people I will be glorified. And Aaron held his peace.

note.label: Leviticus 10: Strange Fire and the Charge of the Priesthood

points: “And Aaron held his peace.” Aaron shut the hell up. He had nothing to say about what the Lord did because they were sacrificing to strange gods, putting strange fire. The Lord made fire shoot out and burnt their behinds up. They were supposed to be the high priests. Setting up incense wasn't out of the ordinary, but they were burning strange fire.

note.label: When Good Intentions Lead To Bad Judgement In Israel

points: Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel the uncle of Aaron, and they came near and carried them in their coats out of the camp, as Moses had said.

note.label: Leviticus 10: Strange Fire and the Charge of the Priesthood

points: Aaron, Eleazar, and Ithamar were told, uncover not your heads, neither rend your clothes, lest ye die and wrath come upon all the people; basically they were told not to mourn for them, because Nadab and Abihu died in the midst of sin and what they did was abominable to the Most High. The whole house of Israel would bewail the burning which the Lord kindled.

note.label: Leviticus 10: Strange Fire and the Charge of the Priesthood

points: Moses told Aaron, Eleazar, and Ithamar to take the meat offering that remained of the offerings made by fire and eat it without leaven beside the altar, in the holy place, for it was their due; and the wave breast and heave shoulder were eaten in a clean place, the due of Aaron and his sons and his daughters by a statute for ever.

note.label: Leviticus 10: Strange Fire and the Charge of the Priesthood

points: Aaron answered Moses: this day have they offered their sin offering and their burnt offering, and such things have befallen me; and if I had eaten the sin offering today, should it have been accepted in the sight of the Lord? And when Moses heard that, he was content.

note.label: Leviticus 10: Strange Fire and the Charge of the Priesthood

points: The priests, the sons of Aaron, were not to be defiled for the dead among their people, except for near kin: mother, father, son, daughter, brother, and a virgin sister that had no husband.

note.label: Leviticus 21: The Holiness of the Priests, the Sons of Aaron

points: A blemish is a disability or birth defect: blind, lame in his walk, a flat nose, any thing superfluous, brokenfooted, brokenhanded, crookbackt, a dwarf, a blemish in the eye, scurvy, scabbed, or stones broken. No man of the seed of Aaron with a blemish could come nigh to offer the offerings of the Lord made by fire.

note.label: Leviticus 21: The Holiness of the Priests, the Sons of Aaron

points: Moses told it unto Aaron, and to his sons, and unto all the children of Israel.

note.label: Leviticus 21: The Holiness of the Priests, the Sons of Aaron

note.label: Leviticus 22: The Holy Things and Offerings Without Blemish

points: It shall be Aaron's and his sons', and they shall eat it in the holy place, for it is most holy unto him of the offerings of the Lord made by fire.

points: The spirit of fear jumped from the leaders onto everybody: all the congregation lifted up their voice and cried, and all the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron. When they murmured against Moses and Aaron, who were they truly murmuring against? The instruction came from the Most High.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

points: All the congregation lifted up their voice and cried, and the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron: would God that we had died in the land of Egypt. Same thing again. Now, mind you, who are they saying this to? God.

note.label: Jude 1:16

points: And all the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron. So, murmuring, complaining, was one of the sins that the children of Israel committed.
We continued to murmur and complain against Moses and Aaron. Against the Lord — which was inevitably against the Lord.

note.label: Resetting Your Joy In The Lord

points: All the congregation lifted up their voice and cried, and the people wept that night, and murmured against Moses and Aaron, saying, Would God that we had died in the land of Egypt, or in this wilderness.

note.label: Numbers 14: The Congregation Rebels and Is Condemned

points: Korah, Dathan, Abiram and On took men, two hundred and fifty princes, famous in the congregation, men of renown with influence, and gathered against Moses and Aaron: ye take too much upon you, seeing all the congregation is holy.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

points: They charged Moses and Aaron with taking too much upon themselves and lifting themselves above the congregation. They thought Moses and Aaron carried themselves as better than the rest, but the Most High is the one who chose them as leaders and was dealing with them; the accusers were jealous of them.

note.label: Numbers 16: The Rebellion of Korah

points: You already stand before the congregation and minister unto them; the Most High is still dealing with you. But they sought the priesthood also, and for that cause Korah and all his company were gathered together against the Lord: and what is Aaron, that ye murmur against him?

note.label: Numbers 16: The Rebellion of Korah

points: Every man took his censer, two hundred and fifty censers, with Aaron and Korah also, put fire and incense in them, and stood in the door of the tabernacle of the congregation; and Korah gathered all the congregation against Moses and Aaron, and the glory of the Lord appeared unto all the congregation.

note.label: Numbers 16: The Rebellion of Korah

points: The plates were a memorial and a sign unto the children of Israel, that no stranger which is not of the seed of Aaron come near to offer incense before the Lord, that he be not as Korah and as his company.

note.label: Numbers 16: The Rebellion of Korah

points: On the morrow, the very next day, all the congregation murmured against Moses and Aaron, saying, ye have killed the people of the Lord. After they had just seen the earth open up and swallow men, they still would not let it go and gathered against Moses again; that is just how rebellious we are.

note.label: Numbers 16: The Rebellion of Korah

points: The Most High saw what was going on, and the cloud covered the tabernacle and the glory of the Lord appeared; Moses and Aaron came before the tabernacle because they knew the Most High was ready to deal with them.

note.label: Numbers 16: The Rebellion of Korah

points: Moses told Aaron to take a censer with fire from off the altar and incense, and go quickly unto the congregation and make an atonement for them, for wrath had gone out from the Lord and the plague was begun; the Most High was already putting them to death.

note.label: Numbers 16: The Rebellion of Korah

points: Aaron ran into the midst of the congregation, put on incense, made an atonement for the people, and stood between the dead and the living; and the plague was stayed.

note.label: Numbers 16: The Rebellion of Korah

points: Every prince gave Moses a rod, one for each according to their fathers' houses, twelve rods, and the rod of Aaron was among them, and Moses laid them up before the Lord in the tabernacle of witness.

note.label: Numbers 17: Aaron's Rod That Budded

points: On the morrow, the rod of Aaron for the house of Levi was budded, and brought forth buds, and bloomed blossoms, and yielded almonds; and every man took back his own rod.

note.label: Numbers 17: Aaron's Rod That Budded

points: The Lord commanded Aaron's rod to be brought again before the testimony, to be kept for a token against the rebels, to take away their murmurings from the Lord, that they die not; so he would not have to put them to death again for murmuring.

note.label: Numbers 17: Aaron's Rod That Budded

points: The Lord told Aaron that he and his sons and his father's house would bear the iniquity of the sanctuary and of their priesthood; that was their job. This explains who should minister in the tabernacle after Israel's cry in the last chapter.

note.label: Numbers 18: The Charge and Portion of the Priests and Levites

points: The Lord gave Aaron the charge of the heave offerings of all the hallowed things of the children of Israel, by reason of the anointing, to him and his sons by an ordinance for ever.

note.label: Numbers 18: The Charge and Portion of the Priests and Levites

points: The Lord told Aaron: thou shalt have no inheritance in their land, neither any part among them; I am thy part and thine inheritance among the children of Israel. The Levites had no inheritance of land to pass down; the Most High said, I will be taking care of you.

note.label: Numbers 18: The Charge and Portion of the Priests and Levites

points: There was no water for the congregation, and the people gathered together against Moses and against Aaron; this is another account of Israel coming against them.

note.label: Numbers 20: Strife at Meribah and Edom's Refusal

points: Moses and Aaron fell upon their faces at the door of the tabernacle, and the glory of the Lord appeared. The command was to take the rod and speak unto the rock before their eyes, and it would give forth his water for the congregation and their beasts.

note.label: Numbers 20: Strife at Meribah and Edom's Refusal

points: At this point Moses got out of the spirit; a stomach can only take so much of a rebellious people. He said, Hear now, ye rebels; must we fetch you water out of this rock? That we is how you know Moses was off: he forgot who was giving the water. It was the Lord giving it, not Moses and not Aaron.

note.label: Numbers 20: Strife at Meribah and Edom's Refusal

points: Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel: for this Moses and Aaron would not bring the congregation into the land given them.

note.label: Numbers 20: Strife at Meribah and Edom's Refusal

points: At mount Hor, by the coast of the land of Edom, the Lord said Aaron shall be gathered unto his people; he could not enter the land because of the rebellion at the water of Meribah.

note.label: Numbers 20: Strife at Meribah and Edom's Refusal

points: Moses stripped Aaron of his garments and put them upon Eleazar his son; the priesthood passed to Eleazar, and Aaron died there in the top of the mount.

note.label: Numbers 20: Strife at Meribah and Edom's Refusal

points: When all the congregation saw that Aaron was dead, all the house of Israel mourned for Aaron thirty days.

note.label: Numbers 20: Strife at Meribah and Edom's Refusal

points: Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, rose up from among the congregation, took a javelin in his hand, and thrust both of them through. And those that died in the plague were 24,000. In one day God killed 24,000, because of sin.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

points: When Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose up from among the congregation, took a javelin in his hand, went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through; so the plague was stayed from the children of Israel, and those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand.

note.label: Numbers 25: Baal-peor and the Zeal of Phinehas

points: Jochebed the daughter of Levi bare unto Amram Aaron and Moses and Miriam their sister; and unto Aaron were born Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

note.label: Numbers 26: The Second Census of the Families of Israel

points: Aaron the priest went up into mount Hor at the commandment of the Lord and died there, in the fortieth year after the children of Israel were come out of the land of Egypt, in the first day of the fifth month; and Aaron was an hundred and twenty and three years old when he died. The number is the fortieth year; read it carefully.

note.label: Numbers 33: The Journeys of Israel from Egypt to the Plains of Moab

points: The Lord was very angry with Aaron to have destroyed him, and Moses prayed for Aaron also at the same time. Moses prayed, and the Lord hearkened unto him; there arose no prophet like Moses, a mighty great man in the scriptures.

note.label: Deuteronomy 9: Not for Thy Righteousness

points: Aaron died and was buried, and Eleazar his son ministered in the priest's office in his stead.

note.label: Deuteronomy 10: What Doth the Lord Require of Thee

points: The cities came out by lot family by family: the children of Aaron the priest, of the Kohathites, had thirteen cities out of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin; the rest of the children of Kohath had ten cities out of Ephraim, Dan, and the half tribe of Manasseh.

note.label: Joshua 21: The Cities of the Levites

points: Eleazar the son of Aaron died, and they buried him in a hill that pertained to Phinehas his son, which was given him in mount Ephraim.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: The ark of the covenant of God was there in those days, and Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, stood before it. They asked, shall I yet again go out to battle against the children of Benjamin my brother, or shall I cease? And the LORD said, go up; for to morrow I will deliver them into thine hand: a direct promise of victory on the morrow.

note.label: Judges 20: Israel's War Against Benjamin

points: When Jacob was come into Egypt and your fathers cried unto the Lord, the Lord sent Moses and Aaron and made Israel dwell in this place. When they forgat the Lord he sold them into the hand of Sisera, captain of the host of Hazor, and of the Philistines, and of the king of Moab; this is the history of the book of Judges, starting in chapter 4.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

points: Aaron and his sons offered upon the altar of burnt offering and the altar of incense and did the work of the place most holy, to make an atonement for Israel according to all that Moses commanded.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 6: The Sons of Levi and the Priesthood

points: The sons of Aaron are named from Eleazar down to Ahimaaz, the high priestly line.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 6: The Sons of Levi and the Priesthood

points: These are the dwelling places of the sons of Aaron and the other Levites, the cities and suburbs given them by lot out of the tribes.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 6: The Sons of Levi and the Priesthood

points: The Levites are named here, for Jehoiada led the Aaronites, the sons of Aaron, and Zadok also was a Levite.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 12: The Tribes Gather to David

points: Concerning Moses the man of God, his sons were named of the tribe of Levi. Aaron was separated that he should sanctify the most holy things, he and his sons forever, to burn incense before the Lord, to minister unto him, and to bless in his name forever. Aaron was set apart specifically for that priestly part, along with all the other Levites who had their different jobs.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 23: The Numbering and Ordering of the Levites

points: Their office was to wait on the sons of Aaron for the service of the house of the Lord, in the courts and the chambers, in the purifying of all holy things, and the work of the shewbread and the fine flour and the offerings. They were to stand every morning to thank and praise the Lord, and likewise at evening, and to offer all burnt sacrifices unto the Lord on the sabbaths, the new moons, and the set feasts, and to keep the charge of the tabernacle and the holy place. This shows the order and what each one's job was in the building and service of the temple.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 23: The Numbering and Ordering of the Levites

points: They had an order and directions on how they were to come into the house of the Lord, according to their manner under Aaron their father, as the Lord God of Israel had commanded them.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 24: The Divisions and Courses of the Priests

points: The rest of the sons of Levi are named after the house of their fathers, family by family, down the line. These likewise cast lots over against their brethren the sons of Aaron in the presence of David the king, and the priests and Levites, even the principal fathers over against their younger brethren.

All these families come from particular bloodlines and particular families that were set over particular things. Just as Aaron's family was already chosen to do the priest's duties of the holy things, each house received its own service as an inheritance, kept in the family.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 24: The Divisions and Courses of the Priests

points: Jeroboam cast out the priests of the Most High, the sons of Aaron and the Levites, and made priests of any man who came to consecrate himself, priests of them that are no gods.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 13: Abijah Stands on the Covenant

points: Judah answers that the Most High is their God and they have not forsaken him; the sons of Aaron minister and the Levites wait upon their business.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 13: Abijah Stands on the Covenant

points: And Azariah the priest went in after him, and with him fourscore priests of the Lord, that were valiant men: and they withstood Uzziah the king, and said unto him, It appertaineth not unto thee, Uzziah, to burn incense unto the Lord, but to the priests the sons of Aaron, that are consecrated to burn incense: go out of the sanctuary; for thou hast trespassed; neither shall it be for thine honour from the Lord God. So he does not want to listen to anybody. The high priest said, what are you doing, that is wrong. And he said, to hell with you, I am the king and God is dealing with me too, I want to burn incense unto my God.

note.label: The Mind of a Child: Void of Ego and Pride

points: And said unto him, It appertaineth not unto thee, Uzziah, to burn incense unto the Lord, but to the priests the sons of Aaron, that are consecrated to burn incense: go out of the sanctuary; for thou hast trespassed; neither shall it be for thine honour from the Lord God. That is not your job to burn incense unto the Lord, that is the priests' job.

note.label: Destructive Behaviors Among Our People

points: Ezra's genealogy is traced back through Zadok and Phinehas to Eleazar the son of Aaron the chief priest, marking him a priest of the true line.

note.label: Ezra 7: Ezra The Ready Scribe Prepares His Heart

points: Moses and Aaron among His priests, and Samuel among them that call upon His name, called upon the Most High and He answered them.
When Moses, Aaron, and Samuel called upon His name, they were keeping the commandments of the Most High. That is why they were answered.

note.label: Psalm 99: The Lord Reigneth, Let the People Tremble

points: They envied Moses also in the camp, and Aaron the saint of the Lord. What were they doing? They despised order. They despised structure. Murmurers, complainers. The earth opened and swallowed up Dathan, and covered the company of Abiram, and the flame burned up the wicked. There was a lesson to be learned in the wilderness. Have we not learned yet?

note.label: Jude 1:16

points: They envied Moses and Aaron the saint of the Lord; the earth swallowed Dathan and the company of Abiram for their insurrection.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

points: O Israel, O house of Aaron, and ye that fear the Lord, trust in the Lord; He is their help and their shield. The Lord has been mindful of us and He will bless us.

note.label: Psalm 115: Not Unto Us, But Unto Thy Name Give Glory

points: It is like the precious ointment upon the head, that ran down upon the beard, even Aaron's beard: that went down to the skirts of his garments. So the Lord compares the unity of our people to the special ointment and oil that was poured upon Aaron's head, that ran down his beard, that only Aaron and his sons could wear. If you copied that ointment or tried to mimic it, you were put to death for that. That is how precious and exclusive that oil was. So God compares our unity to that exclusive anointing oil. Our unity is exclusive. It is special beyond anybody else's unity. Whether it be a European Union, that is garbage in the eyes of God. Or an African summit, that is nonsense in the eyes of God. The unity God seeks is a unity of all twelve tribes of Israel scattered and found throughout the world, especially in the continent of Africa where we are abundant.

note.label: Foundational Babylonian Advocates: Division Among the Dispersion

points: The unity is like the precious ointment upon the head that ran down Aaron's beard to the skirts of his garments, and as the dew of Hermon descending on the mountains of Zion.

note.label: Psalm 133: The Brethren Dwelling Together in Unity
